# Step 2.234, the limits on wrong tries

## Builder 1: the server side

**What exists.** `packages/providers/src/sign-in/limit-subjects.ts` picks the keys a try is counted on: a stranger's on the address and the network; a device the app vouches for on keys of its own (`known-device <id> <address>`, `known-device <id>`), under the same numbers (T-504); wrong codes on `codes <network>`, apart from wrong passwords (T-506). Both adapters use it in `startSignUp`, `startReset`, `verifyCode` and `signIn`, which take an optional `knownDevice` (the vouched device id). The store and the database are unchanged (the keys are text), so no migration. `codesPerHourPerNetwork` is 200, was 30 (T-507). `apps/web/src/server/sign-in/known-device.ts` is the cookie `srl_known`: at each successful sign-in (password, code, Google) an HMAC-SHA-256 tag of the device cookie's id and the address, under a key derived from `SESSION_SECRET` or `SUPABASE_SECRET_KEY` (made up per process without either); http-only, the newest 5 tags, no address or account in it; `flows.ts` vouches only when the device cookie and the address typed give a held tag. Decisions T-504 to T-507 are in `docs/specs/v1/decisions-pending/`; T4 §3 (T-225) is corrected.

**Run and passed.** `npm run check`, `npm run typecheck`, `node --test tests/pending-decisions.test.mjs` (11), `npx vitest run apps/web/src/server/sign-in packages/providers/src/sign-in` (22 files, 328 tests). New: `known-device-limits.test.ts` (6 cases on each adapter: a stranger's ten wrong passwords, the known device's own count, its own code asks, a network's 100 wrong passwords, 31 accounts from one network in an hour with one address still at 5 codes, a bad id thrown), a T-68 case in each `*-identical.test.ts` (answers, and on the Supabase adapter the same calls, store calls and waits), `known-device.test.ts` (5) and four flows cases (the done test's stranger and phone, a copied cookie vouching for nothing, a known device's reset code, T-68 through the limits). Each new test was seen to fail with its code broken by hand, then restored.

**For builder 2 (the screens and the browser proofs).**

- The refusal still comes as `problem=tooManyAttempts&wait=<seconds>`: the screens must say minutes (round up), and name the way in: "Reset your password" on the sign-in screen, and "Continue with Google" where Google is set up (`deps.google`). Do not blame the person ("Too many tries" reads as theirs): say the address is paused for safety.
- The browser proof: sign up on one browser context, sign out, ten wrong passwords from a second context (on the local stand-in every context is one network, so the network count is shared; the address count is what is proved), then the first context signs in, and a third, new one reads minutes and the way in, which works. 31 accounts from one network: through the screens, the bot check's local stand-in passes them.
- The step's bot-check note: a network that filters the bot check's host leaves a signed-out person with only "Continue with Google" or another network. Nothing here opens that door; weigh only words on the screen that say so.
- Messages go in `packages/site/src/messages/en/<area>` files, in alphabetical place.

**For the supervised session (the real adapter).** Supabase Auth's own rate limits (emails sent per hour, OTP and verify per IP) see every request coming from our server's address: set them to at least what T-507 allows, or the 31st parent is refused by Supabase instead of by us. Set `SESSION_SECRET` on the host, so a restart or a second instance keeps the known devices.

**What I distrust.** A stranger's new code for an address replaces the owner's waiting code (one code per address on both adapters, and in GoTrue), so a known device's code can still be killed within its 10 minutes, at the address's 5 an hour. A tag is tied to the address, not the account: after an address moves to another account, an old device keeps its own count for it (never more). `confirmPassword`, `changePassword` and `startEmailChange` still count on the address and network shared with strangers, so a stranger's ten wrong passwords pause a signed-in person's password-again too. The `T-225` row in `DECISIONS.md` and record 013 still say 30 a network: the lead folds T-507 in. Account erasure clears only the plain address's counts; a known device's expire within the hour.

## Builder 2: the screens and the browser proof

**What exists.** A lock-out on the sign-in screen reads "For safety, signing in with a password is paused for N minutes. To get in now, [use "Continue with Google" below, or] choose a new password:" and then a link "Reset your password" (`data-way-in="reset"`, to the forgotten-password route, `next` kept); Google is named only where its button is. Every other pause (sign-up, forgotten password, code, password-again, the account page's forms) reads "For safety, this is paused for N minutes. Please try again after that." (with "or use "Continue with Google" now" where it is drawn). No words say "too many tries"; all the same for an address with an account and one without. `tooManyWords` in `sign-in-parts.tsx` picks the message; the messages are in `en/account.ts`. S-133 (the words, "Decided for you") and T-508 (a network that blocks the bot check gets no way round it; the refusal already names another connection and Google) are pending; T4 §6 and P6 say so. Record 013 now says 200 codes a network (T-507) and the separate counts (T-504, T-506).

**For the lead.** The `T-225` row in `DECISIONS.md` still says "30 per network": fold it to 200 (T-507) when folding T-504 to T-507. T-509 was not used.

**Run and passed.** `npm run check`, `npm run typecheck`, `node --test tests/pending-decisions.test.mjs` (11), `npx vitest run apps/web/src/server/sign-in apps/web/src/features/sign-in packages/site/src/messages` (16 files, 159 tests; three new cases on `tooManyWords`), `npm run test:web` (290). Browser, scripts on: the new `known-device-test` (12 checks, 2 min 45 s, through the runner): sign up, sign out, a stranger's ten wrong passwords, the owner signs in on the phone used before, a new phone reads the 15 minutes and both ways in, and "Reset your password" gets it in. Also `sign-in-says-test` (81, its two lock-out sentences updated), `bot-check-box-test` (41), `script-policy-test` (112). Broken by hand and seen to fail: the sign-in's vouch removed (the owner is refused), the link's words changed (the new phone's step fails), the Google choice inverted (the unit case fails).

**What I distrust.** On the local stand-in every browser is one network, so the browser test proves the address's count, not the network's (the server tests do). The 31-accounts-on-one-network walk was not done in a browser (the server tests cover it). The link sits on its own line under the words (the refusal's links are blocks); it reads well at 390 but was not looked at in a picture.

## The fix round (after the review)

**What exists.** All five of the lead's items, on both adapters. (1, T-509) Every ask for a code, a known device's too, is counted on the address's 5 an hour and the plain network (`codeAskLimits` in `limit-subjects.ts`); a known device is spared only strangers' wrong tries. (2, T-510) A code asked by a known device carries its device id (`sign_in.codes.known_device`, migration 0033); while it works an unknown device's ask makes no `generate_link`, sends no code and replaces nothing, and another's typing answers `code-wrong` and spends nothing. (3) `erase_account` (0033) also removes `known-device <id> <address>` rows; counting any subject now sweeps every row of its scope past its window (`count-code-request.ts`, `guess-counts.ts`), so such rows expire by themselves. (4) Sign-ups are counted apart on the network, 60 an hour (`signUpsPerHourPerNetwork`); the 200 is now sign-in and reset codes. A `flows.test.ts` case signs in to one's own account and then meets another address's lock (Low 6). (5) T-504 amended; T-509, T-510 written; T4's T-225 paragraph corrected.

**Left, by the lead's word.** Low 4: password-again, a new password and a new address still share the address's and the network's count with strangers. Low 5: a known-device tag still never expires.

**Run and passed.** Each new test broken by hand and seen failing (T-509 on both adapters and flows, T-510 replace and spend on both adapters, the database attempt rule, the sweep, the erase, the 60 sign-ups, the tag without its address). `npm run check`, `npm run typecheck`, the sign-in vitest folders (22 files, 331 tests), the database schema, isolation, db, sign-in and erase tests (50 files, 898), `npm run test:real-postgres` (10 files, 94), `known-device-test` (12 checks), `tests/pending-decisions.test.mjs` (11). The whole fence-filter sweep was stopped (30 to 45 minutes, no league query changed; `erase-account.ts` is on its excused list).

**What I distrust.** A stranger typing at a known device's code always hears `code-wrong`, never `too-many-attempts` after five (only the network's count of wrong codes stops them), so a patient stranger could tell that the owner is mid-reset. The sweep deletes by scope and time across subjects: cheap now, worth an index on `asked_at` / `counted_at` at real volume. For the lead: T-507's row still says "200 codes an hour" with no word that sign-ups are now apart (T-509 says it).
